assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Kansai Nerolac Paints (consolidated, Rs crore; Net Profit on the attributable basis via tools/authoring/KANSAINER.patch.js). The company reports one segment (paints), so revenue grows at a single rate and the decorative vs industrial build in businessLines is checked against model revenue in the authoring script. EBITDA margin is a driver. Treasury income = yield x opening cash and investments net of borrowings (incl. leases). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 consolidated +9.8% with ~5% price (MD, 3-Aug-2026 call); Q2 adds ~3% in decorative and 3-5% in industrial as price rises flow through; Diwali falls in November so October is a full painting month. Auto production was very strong in Q1 (SIAM: PV dispatches +25.9%, 2W +20.3%) but laps the post-GST-cut surge from Oct-2025. FY28-29: price laps; decorative grows ~5% (low-single-digit volume, mix up, intense competition), industrial ~9% (auto, powder, performance coatings; new auto/powder capacity from ~FY28-29). Weighted: +10.2% / +7.2% / +7.3%. Below ICICI Securities (+12.1% / +9.6%), close to MNCL (~8% CAGR FY26-28).

base._why: FY26 consolidated revenue Rs8,052 cr split 45:55 using the MD's words at the Kansai Paint India strategy briefing (26-Feb-2026): 'roughly 45% is the total decorative business out of our total company' and 'we are now more than 50% industrial and about 45% to 50% decorative'. In Nov-2024 the company still described itself as 'generally 55% decorative, 45% industrial'. The split is approximate; the company does not report it.

businessLines._why: Decorative: Q1FY27 value growth high single digit (volume low single digit, price ~5%); +8% in FY27 with the Q2 price rise, then +5% as price laps and Birla Opus and JSW Dulux keep competition intense (management: intensity 'continues to remain intact'). Industrial: Q1FY27 double digit (auto, powder and performance coatings strong, auto refinish flat), price rises lag by 1-2 quarters; +12% in FY27, then +9% (management: double-digit growth aim in performance coatings; auto 8-11% a year with SUV mix and exports). The script checks that the two lines sum to model revenue.

assumptions._marginWhy: Consolidated EBITDA margin: 13.2% (FY24), 12.0% (FY25), 12.1% (FY26); Q1FY27 13.8% (14.0%) on low-cost inventory and ~5% price. Management guides 13-14% for FY27 (a range it has repeated for years while delivering 12.7-13.8% standalone and 12-13% consolidated) and aims for '14%+' in 2-3 years. Q2 carries high-cost inventory and industrial pass-through lags; raw materials eased after the June peak. Consolidated runs ~0.6 pts below standalone because of the loss-making Bangladesh subsidiary. We give part credit: 12.4% / 12.8% / 13.0%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Normal capex Rs150-200 cr a year (MD, 3-Aug-2026) plus Rs601 cr for automotive, powder and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur over 'about 2 years, 2-plus years' from Aug-2026. FY26 capex Rs230 cr (AR FY26), Rs213 cr in Screener's cash flow.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs228 cr = 5.45% of average gross block (Rs4,187 cr, Screener); Q1FY27 Rs63 cr (Rs252 cr annualised). The engine depreciates capex at once (CWIP held flat), so 5.4% gives Rs~246-290 cr in FY27-29E as the new plants come on stream.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash and investments net of borrowings incl. leases (Rs2,288 cr at Mar-26 on Screener). FY26 treasury income (interest Rs11.0 cr + profit on sale of current investments Rs71.0 cr + fair-value gains Rs47.2 cr = Rs129.2 cr) was ~7.0% of the opening net balance and ~5.5% of average gross cash and investments; debt-fund returns are falling with rates, so 6%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Two items. (1) Non-treasury other income ~Rs8 cr a year (insurance claims, scrap, miscellaneous: Rs16.7 cr in FY26 incl. a Rs15.5 cr insurance claim). (2) The engine has no minority-interest line: the 45% minority in Bangladesh absorbs part of that subsidiary's losses (non-controlling interests -Rs13.6 cr in FY26; Screener 'minority share' +Rs3 cr in Q1FY27), which lifts attributable profit. We add ~Rs10 cr pre-tax (about Rs7-8 cr after tax) so forecast EPS is on the same attributable basis as the patched history.
assumptions._interestWhy: Rs32 cr in FY26 and Rs8 cr in Q1FY27: mainly interest on lease liabilities (Rs206 cr at Mar-26) and small subsidiary loans; no debt-funded capex (CRISIL: funded from internal accruals).
assumptions._taxWhy: Consolidated effective rate 27.7% in FY26 (Rs221 cr on Rs797 cr) and ~27% in Q1FY27; standalone 26.1%. Subsidiary losses (Bangladesh) get no tax credit. The Nerofix merger (appointed date 1-Apr-2025) lets its losses offset standalone profit. 26.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Regular dividend Rs2.50 a share for FY24, FY25 and FY26 (plus Rs1.25 specials in FY24 and FY25 from the Kavesar and Lower Parel land sales). Rs2.50 is 34% of FY26 reported EPS (Rs7.29). We assume 33%, which takes DPS to ~Rs2.9-3.4.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, AAA-rated MNC subsidiary, but earnings swing with the auto cycle and decorative competition: slightly below market sensitivity (Ke 11.9%).
dcf._tgWhy: Paint demand grows with construction, repainting and vehicle output; 5.5% nominal, below the 6% we use for faster-growing franchises because Nerolac is losing decorative share.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~7% to 7% (industry-like growth, no share gain in decorative).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 13%: the bottom of management's 13-14% range; we do not assume the '14%+' aspiration is reached.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex settles at ~2.6% of sales (normal Rs150-200 cr on Rs8,000 cr of sales, plus capacity every few years); depreciation ~2.9% of sales (FY26 2.8%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Auto and industrial keep growing double digit as new capacity comes on stream; decorative competition eases and premium mix lifts value growth to high single digit; margin reaches management's 14% aspiration.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Birla Opus and JSW Dulux take more decorative share (value growth ~2%), the auto cycle cools after the GST-cut surge and OEMs resist price rises; margin slips back towards 11.5%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Kansai Nerolac (PL 25x Jun-28E, MNCL 23x FY28E, Elara 25x FY28E; ICICI Securities DCF = 22x FY28E). 22x: the house forwardMedian since Apr-2021 is 22.8x (FY26 dropped as a trough year), but it is distorted by Rs1,327 cr of land-sale gains in FY24-25 EPS; on EPS before exceptional items the median is 34.6x. Cut by the ~25% de-rating of listed paint peers (Asian Paints, Berger, Indigo vs their five-year median P/E) gives ~26x; on Nerolac's own de-rating (-44%) it would be ~19x. We take the midpoint (~22.7x) and round down because FY27 growth is mostly price: 22x Sep-28E EPS. Bull 26x (sector de-rating only); bear 17x (below its lowest forward P/E since 2021, ~18.7x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 12x Sep-28E EBITDA = roughly its trailing EV/EBITDA at the 30-Sep close (12.6x), near the five-year low (12.5x) and half the 25.9x median since Apr-2021: a no-re-rating check. Bull 14x, bear 10x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.9%, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash.

cover.headline: A strong industrial business tied to a shrinking decorative one: cheap enough to buy, but this is not a compounder
cover.lead: Kansai Nerolac is the 74.96%-owned Indian arm of Kansai Paint (Japan). About 55% of its ₹8,052 cr FY26 revenue is industrial coatings, where it leads automotive paint (~61% share) and powder coatings; about 45% is decorative paint, where it is losing ground to Grasim's Birla Opus (Q1FY27 revenue ₹1,661 cr, more than Nerolac's whole decorative business) and JSW's Dulux. Revenue grew only ~2% a year in FY23-26 and EPS before land-sale gains was flat at ~₹8. FY27 starts better: Q1 revenue +9.8% on ~5% price rises and booming auto output. The street values the stock on **P/E** (PL 25x Jun-28E, MNCL 23x FY28E). We forecast EPS of ₹8.9 in FY27E and ₹9.9 in FY28E, slightly below the street. Applying **22x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹10.3** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with BUY**, with low conviction. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹224, DCF ₹169. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The price already assumes decorative keeps shrinking
arguments.p: At ₹178 the stock trades at 18.1x our FY28E EPS (~15.2x after ₹28 a share of net cash), against a 34.7x median since 2021 on EPS before exceptional items. Its P/E relative to Asian Paints fell from 0.72 (2023) to 0.47. 22x, a midpoint between the sector's and its own de-rating, gives {{dcf.upside|chg}}.

Nerolac supplies ~61% of India's automotive OEM paint (FY24; 61-81% at the seven largest two- and three-wheeler makers), leads powder coatings and grows double digit in performance coatings. Industrial grew double digit in Q1FY27, and a ₹601 cr expansion in auto, powder and resin capacity is under way.

arguments.h: Decorative is a melting ice cube, not a turnaround
arguments.p: Decorative fell from ~55% of revenue (FY24) to ~45% (FY26). In Q1FY27 its volumes grew only low single digit while Birla Opus grew 64%. Management aims to "maintain our position, if not improve" and says competitive intensity "continues to remain intact". We model decorative +8% in FY27 (mostly price) and +5% a year after.

arguments.h: Value stock or value trap? Some of each
arguments.p: Not a classic trap: earnings should grow ~11% a year to FY29E, the balance sheet holds ₹2,591 cr of cash and investments, and the industrial half deserves more than 18.1x. But ROE is ~10%, below a 12% cost of equity, the DCF (₹169) sits below the price, and ₹1,327 cr of land-sale gains flattered FY24-25. The upside is a re-rating call, not a growth call.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether the margin holds at last year's 11.0% while high-cost inventory is used up, and decorative growth after the price rises.
The festive season (Diwali in November gives a full October painting month) and whether decorative volumes recover against Birla Opus and JSW Dulux.
Auto output once the base includes the post-GST-cut surge (from October 2026), and how much of the industrial price rises OEMs accept.
Completion of the Nerofix merger (expected in Q2FY27 per CRISIL) and progress on the ₹601 cr auto, powder and resin capacity.
Raw materials and the rupee: a lasting fall in crude would bring scheme increases or price cuts in decorative.

sections.title: Two businesses under one brand: car and industrial coatings, and house paint

blocks.p: Kansai Nerolac Paints (KNPL) makes paint in nine Indian plants and sells it in two very different ways. **Industrial coatings** (about 55% of FY26 revenue on management's description) are sold directly to factories: paint for cars, two- and three-wheelers, tractors and trucks on the assembly line (where it is No.1), powder coatings for appliances, furniture and auto parts (No.1), liquid "performance" coatings for bridges, railways, coil steel and pre-engineered buildings (No.3), and auto refinish paint for body shops. These are technical, approval-driven sales: Kansai Paint's global technology matters and 200-300 KNPL technicians work on customers' lines. **Decorative paint** (about 45%) is house paint sold through 35,000+ dealers to painters and homeowners under the Nerolac brand (Excel, Impressions, Beauty, Suraksha), plus Perma waterproofing, construction chemicals, wood finishes and a projects business for builders and institutions. Here brand, dealer incentives and painter loyalty decide sales, and Nerolac competes with Asian Paints, Berger, Birla Opus and JSW Dulux.

sections.title: A ₹60,000 cr paint market with two new giants, and an auto coatings niche that is booming

blocks.p: CRISIL put India's organised paint industry at ~₹60,000 cr of revenue in FY25, with the top five companies holding ~85%; decorative paint is 70-75% of the market. Until 2023 decorative was a cosy oligopoly (Asian Paints, Berger, Nerolac, Akzo Nobel's Dulux, Indigo). Then two conglomerates arrived. Grasim launched **Birla Opus** in Feb-2024 with a planned 1,332 million litres a year (a 40% addition to industry capacity) and ₹10,000 cr of investment; it doubled revenue in FY26 to a ~10% share of decorative and booked ₹1,661 cr in Q1FY27 (+64%), claiming the No.3 spot. **JSW Paints** bought control of Akzo Nobel India (Dulux) in Dec-2025. CRISIL counted ~₹10,000 cr of new-entrant capex and industry utilisation of ~70%: there is far more capacity than demand.

Industrial coatings are a different market: technology, approvals and on-site service decide who wins, and multinational groups and their Indian joint ventures dominate (Kansai Paint's own briefing lists seven rivals across auto, refinish, industrial and powder, several of them joint ventures). Demand follows auto production, consumer durables and infrastructure spending. After the GST cuts of Sep-2025, auto output surged: in Apr-Jun 2026 passenger-vehicle dispatches rose 25.9% and two-wheelers 20.3% (SIAM). The cost side is a petrochemical cycle: raw materials are 55-60% of sales, and the West Asia conflict from Feb-2026 pushed crude and solvent prices sharply higher while the rupee hit record lows (~95/US$ in Apr-2026).

sections.title: Decorative: a well-known brand losing scale to better-funded rivals

blocks.p: Decorative is ~45% of revenue (~₹3,623 cr in FY26, our estimate from management's split). Nerolac's brand is well known: the company says it is the No.2 brand in top-of-mind recall and its jingle has run for 30+ years. But brand recall has not turned into growth. Decorative revenue fell in FY25 (low-single-digit decline in Q3FY25), was flat to slightly negative through H1FY26, and recovered only to mid single digit in Q4FY26 and high single digit in Q1FY27, the last mostly on price: volumes grew "low single digit". Over the same period Birla Opus went from launch (Feb-2024) to ~10% of decorative and ₹1,661 cr of revenue in Q1FY27, while Asian Paints, Berger and Indigo grew revenue 12-20% in that quarter.

bullets: **Strategy: defend, focus, premiumise.** Management's six pillars are new products (Paint+, Excel Everlast 20 with a 20-year warranty, Perma NoDamp NXT), projects, construction chemicals, waterproofing and wood finish, branding, influencer programmes and "focused geographies": over-investing in the towns, mainly in the North and East, where it is No.1 or No.2, for "a 2-3 year strategy" (Feb-2026).

**Giving up volume for mix.** Nerolac is deliberately cutting low-margin, high-volume economy items ("we are not participating greatly into low-margin, high-volume items"), so volume grows slower than the market: in Q1FY27 economy grew mid single digit, super-premium double digit.

**Competition is not easing.** "competition intensity continues to remain intact" and, "for this year, at least that intensity will remain"; freebies (extra grammage) withdrawn in some markets, not others; dealer incentives unchanged from last year (Aug-2026). New entrants now have "reached every corner of the country"; the fight has moved from adding dealers to "extraction from the counter".

**Network.** 1,700+ dealers added in Q1FY27 (3,500+ in 9MFY26); 1.2 lakh painters in the loyalty programme; 385 Paint+ zones. Management plans 5-10% network growth a year, far less than the new entrants added.
**Pricing.** Four decorative price rises between 25-Mar and 11-May 2026 (2%, then 5-6% each, "higher single digit" net); about 3% more flowed into Q2FY27.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** decorative is not a turnaround story. The market is recovering, but Nerolac is recovering slower than everyone else, and on Grasim's own data Birla Opus now sells more decorative paint in a quarter than Nerolac does. Management's honest goal is to hold share in its strongholds. We model +8% in FY27 (mostly price) and +5% a year after, so decorative falls to ~42% of revenue by FY29E. In February 2026 an analyst asked whether Kansai would sell the decorative business; the MD said "this is not a call we would like to take", though "evaluations are ongoing".

bullets: **Automotive OEM (No.1).** Share of India's auto OEM paint rose from 58.1% (FY22) to 61.0% (FY24); "50% plus" across autos (MD, Feb-2026). Kansai Paint's Japanese technology, 200-300 technicians on customer lines and no supply failures make it hard to dislodge. Growth comes from vehicle output (Q1FY27: PVs +25.9%, two-wheelers +20.3%), larger SUVs with more paintable area, metallic shades and new areas such as underbody coatings, sealers, alloy wheels and pre-treatment chemicals.

**Powder coatings (No.1).** Leader "for more than two decades"; demand from appliances, ACs, electricals, furniture and auto parts; growth "robust" in Q1FY27 after a soft FY26 (mid single digit in Q4FY26).

**Performance and general industrial liquids (No.3).** Infrastructure, railways, metro, bridges, coil coating and pre-engineered buildings; "very strong growth" in Q1FY27; management targets double-digit growth and wants to be No.1 in non-auto industrial "in next 2 years".
**Auto refinish.** Flat in Q1FY27; shift from solvent-borne to waterborne under way.

**Pricing power is limited.** OEMs negotiate price rises customer by customer, "always with effective date" but with a 1-2 quarter lag; ~5% industrial price in Q1FY27, another 3-5% expected in Q2. CRISIL lists "pricing pressure from auto OEMs" as a key weakness.

**Capex.** ₹601 cr over ~2-2.5 years for auto, powder and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur (+65,880 KL a year of paint and powder, +9,780 KL of resin for in-house auto-paint intermediates), on top of ₹150-200 cr of normal capex. Industrial utilisation is 70-75%; management expects ROCE in line with today's, rising "towards 18%".

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is the half of Nerolac worth owning: a leadership position with technical switching costs, in a market (vehicles, appliances, infrastructure) growing faster than house paint. We model industrial revenue +12% in FY27 and +9% a year after, which takes it to ~58% of revenue by FY29E. The risks: auto growth slows sharply once the post-GST surge is in the base (from October 2026), OEMs squeeze price, and JSW Dulux brings some of Akzo Nobel's industrial range into the fight.

sections.title: Kansai Paint: technology for a small royalty, and a parent that now sets the strategy openly

blocks.p: Kansai Paint Co. (Japan), one of the world's top-10 coatings makers (CRISIL), owns 74.96% of KNPL, the maximum allowed under India's 75% public-shareholding rule. India is one of its most important markets: since Apr-2025 Kansai Paint itself has held India strategy briefings for its own investors, at which KNPL's MD answers their questions. The relationship is cheap for minorities: KNPL paid a royalty of ₹32.7 cr in FY26 (₹28.6 cr in FY25), about 0.4% of standalone revenue, and ₹0.3 cr of technical fees, for access to the group's automotive and industrial technology. In return the parent received ₹227 cr of the ₹303 cr of dividends paid in FY26.

bullets: **The parent's plan.** Kansai Paint's mid-term plan treats decorative as the "stability" pillar and auto plus industrial as the "growth" and "innovation" pillars, with decorative resources shifted "towards where we are strong". It aims to lift KNPL's margin by ~200bp through premiumisation and tighter selling costs.

**Sourcing.** "As a Kansai Group, we have operation in more than 30-odd countries"; intermediates can be sourced from group plants when needed. KNPL makes its own auto-paint resins and is adding resin capacity; it has no plans to integrate into basic raw materials.

**What minorities cannot control.** Strategy for decorative, any decision to exit it, capital allocation of a ₹2,500 cr cash pile and the payout ratio all sit with a parent that owns three-quarters of the shares. We found no sign of a buyback, delisting offer or stake change by 30-Sep-2026.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** unlike some MNC subsidiaries, KNPL is not milked by its parent: the royalty is small and related-party trade is negligible. The parent's influence shows up instead in strategy (a cautious, margin-first decorative stance) and in a conservative balance sheet that keeps too much cash. A bolder parent could unlock value (buy back shares, sell or merge decorative); there is no sign of that yet.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Kansai Nerolac has **a moat in automotive coatings and none worth paying for in decorative**. Auto OEM paint is a technical, approval-driven business where a ~61% share, Kansai Paint's technology and people on the customer's line create real switching costs. Decorative is where most paint profit in India is made, and there Nerolac is a sub-scale follower: its distribution was copied within two years by newcomers with deeper pockets, and it follows rather than sets prices. Group ROE of ~10% says the same thing: the company as a whole does not earn its cost of capital.

sections.title: The June quarter is the best; the monsoon quarter and the industrial-heavy March quarter are the weakest

blocks.p: Decorative paint sells most in April-June (before the monsoon) and October-December (festive repainting); July-September is wet and slow. Industrial demand is steadier, so the mix tilts towards industrial (lower gross margin) in Q2 and Q4. The result is a margin pattern that repeats every year: in FY25-26 about 14-15% in Q1, 11% in Q2, 12% in Q3 and 9-11% in Q4 (consolidated). Q1FY27 was the strongest quarter in two years: revenue +9.8% to ₹2,374 cr, EBITDA margin 13.8% (14.0% a year earlier). Diwali falls in November in 2026, which gives Q3FY27 a full October painting month (it fell in October in 2025).

sections.title: A decade of two halves: 11% growth to FY19, then ~6% a year (mostly price) and flat underlying profit

blocks.p: Kansai Nerolac's consolidated revenue grew from ₹3,505 cr in FY15 to ₹5,424 cr in FY19, about 11.5% a year, with EBITDA margins of 14-18%. Since then it has grown ~6% a year to ₹8,052 cr in FY26, almost all of it in two years: after two flat Covid years came a 26% and 18% price-led jump in FY22-23 as raw-material costs soared, and then three years of 0-3.4% growth (FY24-26) as decorative demand slowed and new rivals arrived. The margin collapsed to 10% in FY22 and has recovered only to 12-13%. Reported profit is misleading: FY24 (₹1,185 cr) and FY25 (₹1,143 cr) include ₹1,327 cr of pre-tax gains from selling land at Kavesar (Thane) and Lower Parel (Mumbai). Before exceptional items, EPS was ₹8.1, ₹8.0 and ₹7.9 in FY24-26: flat.

sections.title: Earnings quality: a clean audit and good cash, but reported EPS has been a poor guide for three years

bullets: **Exceptional items every year.** FY24: +₹661 cr Kavesar land gain; FY25: +₹665 cr Lower Parel land gain less ₹186 cr of subsidiary impairments (standalone); FY26: −₹63 cr (Wage Code ₹45 cr, warehouse fire ₹13 cr, Bangladesh ₹6 cr). Screener books exceptionals inside "other income", so its EPS history (₹14.7 and ₹14.1 in FY24-25) roughly doubles the underlying ₹8.1 and ₹8.0. Our forward P/E work uses EPS before exceptional items for that reason.

**Treasury income is a sixth of profit.** Of ₹146 cr of FY26 other income, ₹129 cr came from the cash pile: interest ₹11 cr, profit on selling mutual-fund units ₹71 cr and fair-value gains ₹47 cr (marked to market). That was 15% of profit before tax and exceptional items; it falls if rates fall or the cash is spent.

**Rebates and discounts.** Revenue is shown after ₹961 cr of discounts, rebates and incentives (10.7% of the ₹8,983 cr contract price; ₹950 cr in FY25). The ratio is lower than at decorative-heavy peers because of the industrial mix (MD). The auditor lists the estimate of this "variable consideration" as a key audit matter.

**Minorities.** The 45% partner in Bangladesh absorbs part of its losses, so attributable profit (₹589 cr in FY26) is above group profit (₹576 cr). Screener's "Net Profit" row is the group figure; our model uses the attributable one (KANSAINER.patch.js), otherwise the share count would be 2% too low.
**Subsidiaries.** ~₹211 cr of impairments in FY24-26 (standalone) on Sri Lanka and Bangladesh; Sri Lanka sold for ~₹5 lakh; Bangladesh's revenue fell 36% in FY26 to ₹91 cr with a ₹27.6 cr loss.

**Cash conversion is good.** Operating cash flow of ₹2,469 cr in FY24-26 compares with ~₹1,944 cr of profit before exceptional items (~127%), helped by lower inventory. Contingent tax claims are small (₹29 cr standalone).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** S R B C & Co's opinion on the FY26 accounts is unmodified, the only key audit matter is the usual one on rebates, and profits convert to cash. The distortions (land gains, impairments, minorities, treasury gains) are all disclosed; investors just need to strip them out. We do.

sections.title: Debt-free, ₹2,600 cr of cash and investments, and working capital coming down

blocks.p: Kansai Nerolac has no meaningful debt: ₹303 cr of "borrowings" at Mar-2026 are mostly lease liabilities (₹206 cr) and small subsidiary lines. Cash and investments rose from ₹628 cr (Mar-2023) to ₹2,591 cr (Mar-2026) as the two land sales and ₹2,470 cr of operating cash over FY24-26 came in; CRISIL counts an unencumbered surplus of over ₹2,500 cr and rates the company AAA. Working capital is heavy but improving: inventory fell from ₹1,729 cr (FY23) to ₹1,530 cr (FY26) and the cash conversion cycle from 94 days (Dec-2024) to 82 days (Dec-2025) on the parent's measure. Receivables keep rising (₹1,467 cr, 67 days on Screener) because industrial customers, especially auto OEMs, pay slowly.

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 Kansai Nerolac generated ₹3,548 cr of operating cash, spent ₹1,222 cr on capex and paid ₹1,330 cr of dividends. Add ₹1,327 cr of pre-tax land gains in FY24-25 and the cash pile rose to ₹2,591 cr at Mar-2026, 18% of the market value at ₹178. Regular dividends stayed at ₹2.50 a share (about a third of underlying EPS); the land sales funded only two ₹1.25 specials (~₹200 cr). Overseas expansion (Sri Lanka, Bangladesh) destroyed value. ROE before exceptionals was ~10% in FY26 (company: 10.3% standalone), dragged down by cash earning ~6%.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a value stock with a value trap inside it

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's automotive-paint leader (~61% OEM share) and powder-coatings leader, with Kansai Paint's technology behind it, attached to a decorative business that is losing ground; no debt, ₹2,591 cr of cash and investments (₹28 a share net), a ~1.6% dividend yield and an ROE of ~10%.

**What you are paying:** 18.1x our FY28E EPS (~15.2x after net cash), against 34.7x on average since 2021 on underlying earnings and 43-47x for Asian Paints and Berger. On the street's method and our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}), but the DCF (₹169) says the price is roughly fair. The case is a partial re-rating as industrial grows to ~58% of sales, not a turnaround in decorative.

blocks.p: **Value or trap?** A value trap is a stock that looks cheap because its earnings are about to shrink. Nerolac's are not: we expect ~11% EPS growth a year to FY29E from price, auto and industrial. But the decorative half has the hallmarks of a trap: three years of no growth, two richer rivals adding capacity, and a management goal of holding share rather than winning it. The cheap multiple is partly deserved. We think the market is pricing the whole company as if it were all decorative; that gap is the opportunity, and it is not large.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Kansai Nerolac Paints (consolidated, Rs crore; Net Profit on the attributable basis via tools/authoring/KANSAINER.patch.js). The company reports one segment (paints), so revenue grows at a single rate and the decorative vs industrial build in businessLines is checked against model revenue in the authoring script. EBITDA margin is a driver. Treasury income = yield x opening cash and investments net of borrowings (incl. leases). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 consolidated +9.8% with ~5% price (MD, 3-Aug-2026 call); Q2 adds ~3% in decorative and 3-5% in industrial as price rises flow through; Diwali falls in November so October is a full painting month. Auto production was very strong in Q1 (SIAM: PV dispatches +25.9%, 2W +20.3%) but laps the post-GST-cut surge from Oct-2025. FY28-29: price laps; decorative grows ~5% (low-single-digit volume, mix up, intense competition), industrial ~9% (auto, powder, performance coatings; new auto/powder capacity from ~FY28-29). Weighted: +10.2% / +7.2% / +7.3%. Below ICICI Securities (+12.1% / +9.6%), close to MNCL (~8% CAGR FY26-28).

base._why: FY26 consolidated revenue Rs8,052 cr split 45:55 using the MD's words at the Kansai Paint India strategy briefing (26-Feb-2026): 'roughly 45% is the total decorative business out of our total company' and 'we are now more than 50% industrial and about 45% to 50% decorative'. In Nov-2024 the company still described itself as 'generally 55% decorative, 45% industrial'. The split is approximate; the company does not report it.

businessLines._why: Decorative: Q1FY27 value growth high single digit (volume low single digit, price ~5%); +8% in FY27 with the Q2 price rise, then +5% as price laps and Birla Opus and JSW Dulux keep competition intense (management: intensity 'continues to remain intact'). Industrial: Q1FY27 double digit (auto, powder and performance coatings strong, auto refinish flat), price rises lag by 1-2 quarters; +12% in FY27, then +9% (management: double-digit growth aim in performance coatings; auto 8-11% a year with SUV mix and exports). The script checks that the two lines sum to model revenue.

assumptions._marginWhy: Consolidated EBITDA margin: 13.2% (FY24), 12.0% (FY25), 12.1% (FY26); Q1FY27 13.8% (14.0%) on low-cost inventory and ~5% price. Management guides 13-14% for FY27 (a range it has repeated for years while delivering 12.7-13.8% standalone and 12-13% consolidated) and aims for '14%+' in 2-3 years. Q2 carries high-cost inventory and industrial pass-through lags; raw materials eased after the June peak. Consolidated runs ~0.6 pts below standalone because of the loss-making Bangladesh subsidiary. We give part credit: 12.4% / 12.8% / 13.0%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Normal capex Rs150-200 cr a year (MD, 3-Aug-2026) plus Rs601 cr for automotive, powder and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur over 'about 2 years, 2-plus years' from Aug-2026. FY26 capex Rs230 cr (AR FY26), Rs213 cr in Screener's cash flow.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs228 cr = 5.45% of average gross block (Rs4,187 cr, Screener); Q1FY27 Rs63 cr (Rs252 cr annualised). The engine depreciates capex at once (CWIP held flat), so 5.4% gives Rs~246-290 cr in FY27-29E as the new plants come on stream.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash and investments net of borrowings incl. leases (Rs2,288 cr at Mar-26 on Screener). FY26 treasury income (interest Rs11.0 cr + profit on sale of current investments Rs71.0 cr + fair-value gains Rs47.2 cr = Rs129.2 cr) was ~7.0% of the opening net balance and ~5.5% of average gross cash and investments; debt-fund returns are falling with rates, so 6%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Two items. (1) Non-treasury other income ~Rs8 cr a year (insurance claims, scrap, miscellaneous: Rs16.7 cr in FY26 incl. a Rs15.5 cr insurance claim). (2) The engine has no minority-interest line: the 45% minority in Bangladesh absorbs part of that subsidiary's losses (non-controlling interests -Rs13.6 cr in FY26; Screener 'minority share' +Rs3 cr in Q1FY27), which lifts attributable profit. We add ~Rs10 cr pre-tax (about Rs7-8 cr after tax) so forecast EPS is on the same attributable basis as the patched history.
assumptions._interestWhy: Rs32 cr in FY26 and Rs8 cr in Q1FY27: mainly interest on lease liabilities (Rs206 cr at Mar-26) and small subsidiary loans; no debt-funded capex (CRISIL: funded from internal accruals).
assumptions._taxWhy: Consolidated effective rate 27.7% in FY26 (Rs221 cr on Rs797 cr) and ~27% in Q1FY27; standalone 26.1%. Subsidiary losses (Bangladesh) get no tax credit. The Nerofix merger (appointed date 1-Apr-2025) lets its losses offset standalone profit. 26.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Regular dividend Rs2.50 a share for FY24, FY25 and FY26 (plus Rs1.25 specials in FY24 and FY25 from the Kavesar and Lower Parel land sales). Rs2.50 is 34% of FY26 reported EPS (Rs7.29). We assume 33%, which takes DPS to ~Rs2.9-3.4.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, AAA-rated MNC subsidiary, but earnings swing with the auto cycle and decorative competition: slightly below market sensitivity (Ke 11.9%).
dcf._tgWhy: Paint demand grows with construction, repainting and vehicle output; 5.5% nominal, below the 6% we use for faster-growing franchises because Nerolac is losing decorative share.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~7% to 7% (industry-like growth, no share gain in decorative).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 13%: the bottom of management's 13-14% range; we do not assume the '14%+' aspiration is reached.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex settles at ~2.6% of sales (normal Rs150-200 cr on Rs8,000 cr of sales, plus capacity every few years); depreciation ~2.9% of sales (FY26 2.8%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Auto and industrial keep growing double digit as new capacity comes on stream; decorative competition eases and premium mix lifts value growth to high single digit; margin reaches management's 14% aspiration.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Birla Opus and JSW Dulux take more decorative share (value growth ~2%), the auto cycle cools after the GST-cut surge and OEMs resist price rises; margin slips back towards 11.5%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Kansai Nerolac (PL 25x Jun-28E, MNCL 23x FY28E, Elara 25x FY28E; ICICI Securities DCF = 22x FY28E). 22x: the house forwardMedian since Apr-2021 is 22.8x (FY26 dropped as a trough year), but it is distorted by Rs1,327 cr of land-sale gains in FY24-25 EPS; on EPS before exceptional items the median is 34.6x. Cut by the ~25% de-rating of listed paint peers (Asian Paints, Berger, Indigo vs their five-year median P/E) gives ~26x; on Nerolac's own de-rating (-44%) it would be ~19x. We take the midpoint (~22.7x) and round down because FY27 growth is mostly price: 22x Sep-28E EPS. Bull 26x (sector de-rating only); bear 17x (below its lowest forward P/E since 2021, ~18.7x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 12x Sep-28E EBITDA = roughly its trailing EV/EBITDA at the 30-Sep close (12.6x), near the five-year low (12.5x) and half the 25.9x median since Apr-2021: a no-re-rating check. Bull 14x, bear 10x.
